title: Understanding an Investment Banking Salary: Award Rates, National Minimum Wage, and Hourly Conversion
description: Learn how to convert an hourly rate to annual pay for an investment banking salary using Fair Work award rates, the National Minimum Wage, and the 38-hour week. Includes tax and su
salarySummary: For a full-time employee under the Banking, Finance and Insurance Award, a Level 1 hourly rate of $26.97 works out to $53,284 per year based on 38 hours per week, with super and tax calculated on top.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to an annual salary for an investment banking role?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then multiply by 52. For a full-time employee under the Banking, Finance and Insurance Award, the standard is 38 hours per week. For example, a Level 1 hourly rate of $26.97 gives $26.97 × 38 × 52 = $53,284 per year. This is the base salary before super and tax. Actual investment banking salaries are often much higher than award minimums, but the conversion method remains the same.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates for investment banking?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week. However, employees in the banking, finance and insurance industry are covered by the Banking, Finance and Insurance Award 2020, which sets higher minimum rates. For example, a Level 1 employee must be paid at least $26.97 per hour, and a Level 6 employee at least $38.07 per hour. Award rates also include penalty rates, allowances, and casual loading. Actual investment banking salaries typically exceed these award minimums.

faqs.q: Does the investment banking salary include superannuation?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of the base salary. Under the Superannuation Guarantee, employers must contribute 12% of ordinary earnings (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830) into a super fund. For a Level 1 employee earning $53,284 per year, the super contribution would be approximately $6,394, making total employment cost $59,678. The base salary is the figure used for hourly conversion and tax calculations.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting an Hourly Rate to an Annual Investment Banking Salary

When you see an hourly rate for a job in banking, finance or insurance, the first question is often: *What does that mean as an annual salary?* The answer is straightforward: multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For full-time employees under the **Banking, Finance and Insurance Award 2020** (the award), the standard ordinary hours are 38 per week. So the formula is:

**Annual gross salary = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, the award’s Level 1 minimum hourly rate from 1 July 2026 is $26.97. That gives $26.97 × 38 × 52 = **$53,284 per year**. If you are paid fortnightly, your gross pay would be the weekly rate ($1,024.70) multiplied by two, or **$2,049.40 per fortnight**.

### Award Rates vs. the National Minimum Wage

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, the award sets higher minimums for the banking, finance and insurance industry. The award has six classification levels, each with its own minimum hourly rate:

| Classification | Hourly rate | Weekly rate | Annual salary (38 hours × 52 weeks) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Level 1 | $26.97 | $1,024.70 | $53,284 |
| Level 2 | $29.45 | $1,119.10 | $58,193 |
| Level 3 | $31.11 | $1,182.10 | $61,469 |
| Level 4 | $32.67 | $1,241.40 | $64,553 |
| Level 5 | $33.99 | $1,291.80 | $67,174 |
| Level 6 | $38.07 | $1,446.80 | $75,234 |

These are the **minimum** rates. Actual investment banking salaries are typically much higher, but the award provides the legal baseline. For more detail on how these rates apply, see the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you are a casual employee, you receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For a Level 1 casual, that’s $26.97 × 1.25 = **$33.71 per hour**. This loading replaces entitlements like annual leave and sick leave. You can use [the timesheet](/) to calculate your pay with or without casual loading.

Superannuation is paid **on top** of your base salary. Under the Superannuation Guarantee, your employer must contribute 12% of your ordinary earnings (up to $270,830 per year) into a super fund. For a Level 1 employee earning $53,284, that’s an extra $6,394 per year. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary packaging can affect your take-home pay.

### Tax on Your Investment Banking Salary

Once you have your annual gross salary, you can estimate your tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for lower incomes). For a Level 1 salary of $53,284, the tax would be approximately $7,088 plus Medicare $1,066, leaving about **$45,130 take-home pay** (excluding HELP or Medicare levy surcharge). Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more personalised estimate.

### How This Applies to Investment Banking

While the award rates above are the legal minimums, investment banking salaries in Australia are often significantly higher, especially for analysts and associates. The **Australian Bureau of Statistics** reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026, which equates to about $108,352 per year. Investment banking roles frequently exceed this average. However, the conversion method remains the same: hourly rate × hours per week × 52.

If you are comparing a salary offer, remember that the award also includes penalty rates for overtime, weekend work, and public holidays. For a full breakdown of penalty rates, see the [reference tables](/data) on our site.

### Important Notes on the Conversion

- The calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week with no unpaid overtime.
- It does not include penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base.
- Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here.
- This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more information on the National Minimum Wage and award rates, visit the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page. To convert your own hourly rate to annual pay, use [the timesheet](/) calculator.
